claims.text: Oxidizing-gas exposure at elevated temperature accelerates degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Oxidation promotes coarsening and interconnection of Cr-rich nitride and sigma-phase precipitates at grain boundaries.
Coarsened, interconnected grain-boundary precipitates reduce grain-boundary cohesion and lead to catastrophic failure under mechanical stress.
Reducing conditions suppress oxidation-driven precipitate growth and preserve mechanical integrity.
The as-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-manufactured alloy contains fine Cr-rich nitride and sigma-phase precipitates.
The as-manufactured alloy is a supersaturated solid solution.
Changing the annealing atmosphere from inert or reducing to oxidizing is the proposed controlled intervention.
Cr-rich nitride and sigma-phase precipitates grow during prolonged exposure between approximately 900 K and 1300 K.
Grain-boundary oxide or oxide-nitride layers form under oxidizing exposure and compromise cohesion.
Oxygen reacts preferentially at grain boundaries and with chromium in this alloy.
Preferential oxidation accelerates nucleation and growth of coarse brittle precipitates and produces interconnected oxide networks.
Secondary-phase precipitation can alter mechanical properties and may embrittle an FCC high-entropy alloy.
Oxidized samples will show larger and more continuous grain-boundary precipitates than both the as-manufactured baseline and reducing-atmosphere controls.
Oxidized samples will have markedly lower microhardness than the baseline and reducing-atmosphere controls.
Oxidized samples will have markedly lower fracture toughness than the baseline and reducing-atmosphere controls.
The starting state has a homogeneous fine precipitate distribution and intact grain boundaries.
Above approximately 1300 K, the alloy may revert toward a single FCC structure as nitride and sigma phases disappear.
Below approximately 900 K, oxidation may be too slow for the proposed degradation mechanism to apply.
The oxidation-driven mechanism is falsified if oxidizing exposure produces neither greater precipitate or oxide development nor lower mechanical properties than the reducing-atmosphere control.
